items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I actually was trying to emulate Coleman Hawkins to a degree, because he had just finished working with Hawkins, and he had told me about how this song...he could imagine Hawk doing it, you know. So I tried to emulate Coleman Hawkins to a degree on 'Deep Meditation.'

ctx.x: But one of my favorites was Earl Fatha Hines. My Aunt Lydia... We used to go to dances together all the time, because my uncle, he didn't care anything about that, you know. We'd always go. And her favorite saxophone player was Budd Johnson. And whenever Earl Hines came down, she'd say, 'Let's go hear Mister Johnson.' They came out with that record, 'Please, Mister Johnson'... Ha-ha, that was something beautiful, you know, to see Eckstine and Madeleine Green and all those people, you know.

It was really a treat to have these outlets where you could go and hear people. It just opened you up so much, you know. Coleman Hawkins came through there after he came from Europe; he played the Graystone Ballroom. And 'Body and Soul' was on all the jukeboxes. You know, his classic; it was on all of the jukeboxes. It was really something special.
